record.reference: Shepherd of Hermas — Vision 4, section iii

source.text: Ἠρώτησα αὐτὴν περὶ τῶν τεσσάρων χρωμάτων ὧν εἶχεν τὸ θηρίον εἰς τὴν κεφαλήν. ἡ δὲ ἀποκριθεῖσά μοι λέγει· Πάλιν περίεργος εἶ περὶ τοιούτων πραγμάτων. Ναί, φημί, κυρία· γνώρισόν μοι τί ἐστιν ταῦτα. 2. Ἄκουε, φησίν· τὸ μὲν μέλαν οὗτος ὁ κόσμος ἐστίν, ἐν ᾧ κατοικεῖτε. 3. τὸ δὲ πυροειδὲς καὶ αἱματῶδες, ὅτι δεῖ τὸν κόσμον τοῦτον δι' αἵματος καὶ πυρὸς ἀπόλλυσθαι· 4. τὸ δὲ χρυσοῦν μέρος ὑμεῖς ἐστὲ οἱ ἐκφυγόντες τὸν κόσμον τοῦτον. ὥσπερ γὰρ τὸ χρυσίον δοκιμάζεται διὰ τοῦ πυρὸς καὶ εὔχρηστον γίνεται, οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς δοκιμάζεσθε [οἱ κατοικοῦντες] ἐν αὐτοῖς. οἱ οὖν μείναντες καὶ πυρωθέντες ὑπ' αὐτοῦ καθαρισθήσεσθε. ὥσπερ τὸ χρυσίον ἀποβάλλει τὴν σκωρίαν αὐτοῦ, οὕτω καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀποβαλεῖτε πᾶσαν λύπην καὶ στενοχωρίαν, καὶ καθαρισθήσεσθε καὶ χρήσιμοι ἔσεσθε εἰς τὴν οἰκοδομὴν τοῦ πύργου. 5. τὸ δὲ λευκὸν μέρος ὁ αἰὼν ὁ ἐπερχόμενός ἐστιν, ἐν ᾧ κατοικήσουσιν οἱ ἐκλεκτοὶ τοῦ θεοῦ· ὅτι ἄσπιλοι καὶ καθαροὶ ἔσονται οἱ ἐκλελεγμένοι ὑπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον. 6. σὺ οὖν μὴ διαλίπῃς λαλῶν εἰς τὰ ὦτα τῶν ἁγίων. ἔχετε καὶ τὸν τύπον τῆς θλίψεως τῆς ἐρχομένης μεγάλης. ἐὰν δὲ ὑμεῖς θελήσητε, οὐδὲν ἔσται. μνημονεύετε τὰ προγεγραμμένα. 7. ταῦτα εἴπασα ἀπῆλθεν, καὶ οὐκ εἶδον ποίῳ τόπῳ ἀπῆλθεν· ψόφος γὰρ ἐγένετο· κἀγὼ ἐπεστράφην εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω φοβηθείς, δοκῶν ὅτι τὸ θηρίον ἔρχεται.
source.label: Vision 4, section iii

translation.text:
I asked her about the four colors that the beast had upon its head[a]. But she answered me and says, "Again you are curious about such matters." "Yes, my Lady," I say; "make known to me what these things are."

She says, "Listen: the black is this world, in which you dwell. And the fiery and blood-red is because this world must be destroyed by blood and fire. But the golden portion is you who have escaped this world. For just as gold is tested by fire and becomes useful, so also you are being tested among them[e]. Therefore, those who remain and are fired by it[f] will be purified. Just as gold casts off its dross, so also you will cast off every grief and distress, and you will be purified and will be useful for the building of the tower.

"But the white portion is the age that is coming, in which the elect of God will dwell; because those chosen by God for eternal life will be spotless and pure.

"You, therefore, do not cease speaking in the ears of the holy ones. You also have the pattern of the great tribulation that is coming; but if you are willing, it will be nothing. Remember the things written beforehand."

Having said these things, she went away, and I did not see to what place she went; for a noise occurred. And I turned around in fear[o][n][m][l][k][j][i][h][f][e][c][b], thinking that the beast was coming.

footnotes.text: Greek κυρία. 'Lady' keeps respectful address without connotations of ownership that 'Mistress' may carry.
Greek πυροειδὲς καὶ αἱματῶδες: 'fiery and blood‑red.' Alternatives: 'fiery and blood‑stained' or 'blood‑colored.'

The phrase reads 'so also you are being tested in/among them (ἐν αὐτοῖς)'. Some witnesses include 'those who dwell' ([οἱ κατοικοῦντες]), yielding 'you who dwell among them.' The referent of 'them' may be the elements/events just mentioned (blood, fire) or the conditions of this world.
'Fired by it' follows the metallurgical metaphor; 'it' most naturally refers to the fire/testing process.
Cross‑reference: the tower vision throughout Visions 3–4, where stones are prepared for building.
Greek αἰὼν ὁ ἐπερχόμενος: 'the age that is coming.' Alternative: 'the world to come.'
Greek ἅγιοι: rendered 'holy ones' rather than 'saints' to preserve early-Christian diction.
Greek θλῖψις μεγάλη ἐρχομένη: 'the great tribulation that is coming.' Alternative: 'the coming great distress/affliction.'

'If you are willing, it will be nothing' may mean the trial’s impact will be as nothing for those prepared; alternative understanding: 'if you are willing, nothing will happen' (the event is averted).
'The things written beforehand' (τὰ προγεγραμμένα) likely refers to earlier written admonitions or previously revealed parts of the vision.
Greek ψόφος: 'noise' or 'sound', an unspecified disturbance.

lexical_decisions.rationale: Common apocalyptic term; "beast" preserves symbolic weight without adding 'wild' unless needed.
Plain sense of visible hues on the beast’s head.
Spatial prepositional sense; "upon" keeps the visionary concreteness.
Reproach for inquisitiveness fits context; 'curious' is idiomatic yet close to sense.
Hermas consistently addresses the visionary woman as 'Lady'; 'Mistress' can imply ownership and is less fitting in English.
Here denotes the present human world-order in which they dwell; 'world' captures this.
Adjectival form meaning 'of fire-like appearance'.
Color nuance fits the symbolic palette; 'blood‑red' is succinct.
Passive infinitive of ruin fits prophetic-apocalyptic diction.
'Golden portion' keeps the metaphor; 'gold' for the refining comparison.
Compound emphasizes deliverance from; 'escaped' is natural English.
Metallurgical testing; 'tested' communicates the process.
Outcome of testing is suitability for use; 'useful' is clear and concise.
Keeps the ambiguity of the Greek referent (the conditions or elements mentioned).
Metallurgical 'to fire' matches the gold-smelting imagery.
Standard term for impurities removed in refining.
Emotional burden to be cast off; 'grief' pairs well with 'distress'.
Captures constriction/pressure metaphor in accessible English.
Echoes earlier εὔχρηστον to keep the utility motif consistent.
Literal building of the symbolic tower, not abstract 'edification' here.
Color in the symbolic sequence; plain rendering.
'Age' reflects two-age eschatology; 'coming' keeps the temporal movement.
Adjectival form as 'elect'; participle as 'those chosen' to reflect aspect while keeping root consistency.
Idiomatic pair in moral purity language.
'Holy ones' preserves early-Christian texture and literal sense.
'Pattern' conveys an exemplar/foreshadow without technical theological 'type' jargon.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the great tribulation that is coming
alternatives: the great distress that is coming
lexical_decisions.rationale: 'Tribulation' preserves apocalyptic register while remaining intelligible.
Plain imperative; keeps pro- prefix nuance of prior recording.
Neutral auditory disturbance fits the scene.
Natural English for physical movement to the rear.
Cognitive aspect of the narrator’s fear.

theological_decisions.issue: Rendering of αἰών in eschatological context
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Translate αἰών as 'age' in 'the age that is coming'.
theological_decisions.rationale: Hermas uses apocalyptic two-age framework; 'age' preserves that, whereas 'world' risks conflating with κόσμος already used for the present order.

theological_decisions.issue: Interpretation of 'ἐὰν δὲ ὑμεῖς θελήσητε, οὐδὲν ἔσται'
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Render 'if you are willing, it will be nothing' (i.e., the coming tribulation will be as nothing for you).
alternative_readings: 'If you are willing, nothing will happen' (the event is averted)
'If you are willing, there will be nothing' (elliptical)
theological_decisions.rationale: Immediate context urges admonition and remembrance, implying preparation and endurance. The sense that the trial’s impact is nullified for the willing fits Hermas’ paraenetic pattern better than cancellation of the event.
'Holy ones' is a transparent gloss preserving early-Christian diction and avoids later ecclesiastical coloration.
'Tribulation' maintains apocalyptic register consistent with the visionary genre and the intensifier 'great'.

theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Use 'elect' for ἐκλεκτοί and 'those chosen' for ἐκλελεγμένοι.
theological_decisions.rationale: Maintains root consistency while reflecting grammatical differences (adjective vs participle), and keeps the sentence readable.

review_passes.summary: The draft is generally excellent but flattens several historical presents into past tense, misses a couple of conjunctions (δὲ, οὖν), and uses inconsistent English verbs for the repeated Greek verb ἀποβάλλω.
issues_found: In verse 1, the draft translates the historical presents λέγει and φημί as past tense ('said'), losing the vividness of the dialogue. It also misses the conjunction δὲ ('But').
In verse 4, the draft omits the inferential conjunction οὖν ('So' or 'Therefore') in 'οἱ οὖν μείναντες'.
In verse 4, the draft translates ἀποβάλλει as 'casts off' and ἀποβαλεῖτε as 'throw off'. Harmonizing to 'cast off' preserves the author's deliberate repetition.
In verse 4, the draft translates ὥσπερ as 'As', whereas earlier in the verse it was translated as 'just as'. Harmonizing to 'Just as' improves consistency.

revision_pass.changes_summary: doctrine_realignment: HERM.V.4 upon its head / among them / fired by it. Restored 3 chosen renderings preserving visionary concreteness, deliberate ambiguity of ἐν αὐτοῖς, and metallurgical 'fired' register.

revisions.from:
I asked her about the four colors which the beast[a] had upon its head. But she answered me and says, "Again you are being curious about such matters." "Yes, my Lady,[b]" I say; "make known to me what these things are."

She says, "Listen: the black is this world in which you dwell. And the fiery and blood‑red[c]—that is because this world must be destroyed through blood and fire. But the golden portion is you who have escaped this world. For just as gold is tested by fire and becomes useful, so also you are being tested among them[e]. So those of you who remain and are fired by it[f] will be purified. Just as gold casts off its dross, so also you will cast off every grief and distress, and you will be purified and be useful for the building of the tower[h].

"But the white portion is the age that is coming[i], in which the elect of God will dwell; because those chosen by God for eternal life will be spotless and pure.

"You, therefore, do not cease speaking into the ears of the holy ones[j]. You also have the pattern[k] of the great tribulation that is coming[l]; but if you are willing, it will be nothing[m]. Remember the things written beforehand[n]."

Having said these things, she went away, and I did not see to what place she went; for a noise occurred[o]. And I turned around in fear, thinking that the beast was coming.

revisions.rationale: Adjusted several renderings for closer lexical accuracy and more natural formal English: 'which' to 'that,' 'upon' to 'on,' 'being curious' to 'are curious,' added comma after 'world,' changed 'through' to 'by' for διὰ, rendered ἐν αὐτοῖς as 'in them' rather than interpretive 'among them,' changed 'fired by it' to 'burned by it,' smoothed future sequence to 'will be useful,' changed 'into the ears' to 'in the ears,' and removed footnote markers.

Ἄκουε, φησίν· τὸ μὲν μέλαν οὗτος ὁ κόσμος ἐστίν, ἐν ᾧ κατοικεῖτε. 3. τὸ δὲ πυροειδὲς καὶ αἱματῶδες, ὅτι δεῖ τὸν κόσμον τοῦτον δι' αἵματος καὶ πυρὸς ἀπόλλυσθαι· 4. τὸ δὲ χρυσοῦν μέρος ὑμεῖς ἐστὲ οἱ ἐκφυγόντες τὸν κόσμον τοῦτον. ὥσπερ γὰρ τὸ χρυσίον δοκιμάζεται διὰ τοῦ πυρὸς καὶ εὔχρηστον γίνεται, οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς δοκιμάζεσθε [οἱ κατοικοῦντες] ἐν αὐτοῖς. οἱ οὖν μείναντες καὶ πυρωθέντες ὑπ' αὐτοῦ καθαρισθήσεσθε. ὥσπερ τὸ χρυσίον ἀποβάλλει τὴν σκωρίαν αὐτοῦ, οὕτω καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀποβαλεῖτε πᾶσαν λύπην καὶ στενοχωρίαν, καὶ καθαρισθήσεσθε καὶ χρήσιμοι ἔσεσθε εἰς τὴν οἰκοδομὴν τοῦ πύργου. 5. τὸ δὲ λευκὸν μέρος ὁ αἰὼν ὁ ἐπερχόμενός ἐστιν, ἐν ᾧ κατοικήσουσιν οἱ ἐκλεκτοὶ τοῦ θεοῦ· ὅτι ἄσπιλοι καὶ καθαροὶ ἔσονται οἱ ἐκλελεγμένοι ὑπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον. 6. σὺ οὖν μὴ διαλίπῃς λαλῶν εἰς τὰ ὦτα τῶν ἁγίων. ἔχετε καὶ τὸν τύπον τῆς θλίψεως τῆς ἐρχομένης μεγάλης. ἐὰν δὲ ὑμεῖς θελήσητε, οὐδὲν ἔσται. μνημονεύετε τὰ προγεγραμμένα. 7. ταῦτα εἴπασα ἀπῆλθεν, καὶ οὐκ εἶδον ποίῳ τόπῳ ἀπῆλθεν· ψόφος γὰρ ἐγένετο· κἀγὼ ἐπεστράφην εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω φοβηθείς, δοκῶν ὅτι τὸ θηρίον ἔρχεται.

base_translation.text: She says, "Listen: the black is this world, in which you dwell. And the fiery and blood-red is because this world must be destroyed by blood and fire. But the golden portion is you who have escaped this world. For just as gold is tested by fire and becomes useful, so also you are being tested in them. Therefore, those who remain and are burned by it will be purified. Just as gold casts off its dross, so also you will cast off every grief and distress, and you will be purified and will be useful for the building of the tower.

translation.text:
She says, “Listen. The black part represents this world, where you live. The fiery, blood-red part means that this world must be destroyed by blood and fire. But the gold part represents you who have escaped from this world.

“Gold is tested by fire so that it becomes useful. In the same way, you are being tested in these things. Those who remain and are burned by the fire will be purified. Just as gold sheds its impurities, you too will shed every grief and distress. You will be purified and made useful for building the tower.”

She says, “Listen. The black part represents this world, where you live. The fiery, blood-red part means that this world must be destroyed by blood and fire. But the gold part represents you who have escaped from this world.

“Gold is tested by fire so that it becomes useful. In the same way, you are being tested through these trials. Those who stand firm while the fire burns them will be purified. Just as gold sheds its impurities, you too will shed every grief and distress. You will be purified and made useful for building the tower.”
spob_revision_history.review_summary: The draft usefully explains the colors as symbolic and replaces “dross” with the clear equivalent “impurities.” However, “stand firm” adds a specific exhortational sense beyond “remain,” and “these trials” resolves a still-broad antecedent more narrowly than necessary. The recommended revision preserves the helpful clarity while retaining the passage’s wording and scope.
